poc_plan:
Objective: validate Dedicated capacity sizing and SLO commitments for latency-sensitive fraud and chat workloads.
Scope: two-week POC in Redwood Dedicated staging (VPC peered network) with representative traffic: 1) real-time fraud scoring (batchable stream) 2) customer support short-chat flows (avg 30-120 tokens).
Workloads: synthetic replay of 3M events/day condensed to test windows, + live QA traffic. Tests: ramped load test to target sustained QPS; 6h soak at target QPS; stress bursts to 2x expected; failover and model fallback exercises.
Acceptance criteria: p95 < 180ms for 32-token replies (chat), p99 < 420ms for 128-token completion under steady-state; sustained throughput 400 req/s for chat workflows; 99.9% availability during soak (no model OOMs).
Instrumentation: capture per-request p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, queue depth, and tokens/sec. Test harness: JMeter + internal replay tool; logs stored to drive link.
Artifacts: load scripts, sample prompt sets, expected-slot mapping, and cost model projection.
Decision gate: Recommend reserved capacity commit if POC meets acceptance + legal SLA redlines accepted.
benchmark_results_summary:
Key outcome from staging runs:
- Peak ramp test: achieved 520 req/s for short-chat (<=64 tokens) for 5 minutes; average p95=200ms, p99=380ms.
- Soak test (6h) at 420 req/s: sustained with average GPU util 72%, cache hit rate 48%; three tail spikes correlated to tokenization variability and a single large prompt.
- Fraud scoring (batch stream): reached 2.1M tokens/min using batching/kv prefix caching with avg latency 110ms for scalar score call.
- Failure modes: single-worker OOM when a 5k-token ingestion hit a worker — mitigated by request size limits and adaptive batching.
- Fallback policy test: auto-route to quantized model (half-precision) under simulated capacity pressure — observed 18% latency increase but preserved availability.
Recommendation: Reserve 8x A100-80GB or 12x A10s for initial prod; enable KV prefix caching and small-request size caps; include explicit SLO credit table for p99 misses and warm-up window during deploys.
technical_requirements:
Requested SLOs: p95 and p99 percentiles with service credits; dedicated worker pools with no noisy neighbor; KMS HSM support and rotation policy; VPC peering and private egress; audit logging retention 7 years (archival).
Model preferences: smaller tuned LLM for score generation (fine-tuned Llama-variant) + higher-capacity open model for agent responses; want model pinning per route and automatic fallback to quantized variant.
Capacity ask: current projection for peak production is 700 req/s for chat plus batch scoring bursts (3M tokens/day). They prefer guidance on GPU equivalency and expected headroom for 99th percentile traffic spikes.
